text.p: A leader of ETA's political arm Herri Batasuna (HB) was found dead in his home in the Basque town of Mallabia, the Civil Guard said on Monday.
Eugenio Aranburu was due to appear in Spain's Supreme Court at 5 p.m. (1600 GMT) to answer charges he and other HB leaders promoted violence.
Aranaburu, 41, was found hanged at 1 p.m. (1200 GMT), but the Basque police did not say whether it was suicide. They said they were still investigating the cause of death.
Five members of HB's 25-person leadership were sent to prison last week for failing to appear before the Supreme Court.
On Saturday, HB members held a news conference urging demonstrations and strikes to protest at the jailings.

HB, which does not renounce violence as a means of acheiving Basque independence, is charged with distributing a videotape that promotes the violent separatist rebel group ETA. ETA, which has murdered some 800 people since starting its drive for independence in 1968, was blamed for a car bomb earlier on Monday that killed one man.
